answer: A tide gauge reader log is the credential: gauges read at one harbour across years of tides. Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The ocean signal separates the two cases at a glance: The cost lands per head: 396 aliases need 396 records, each checked live against the issuer, so bulk forgery costs 396 times what one honest seat costs. The zephyr ledger records each payment, the opal window resets the board, and 396 fakes never beat one honest agent on price.
